messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 tail latency for customer 'GalaxyHome' exceeded SLO on streaming API (p99 ~ 3.4s -> 9.8s). Impact: some single-tenant streaming sessions showing stalls. paging: @eric_oncall (primary)

eric_oncall: paging in. grabbing logs now. any immediate mitigation suggestions? :rotating_light:

anya_sre: saw a brief p95 jump first, then p99 exploded. looks like many long-prefix prompts + high concurrency from a single API key. could be KV cache churn.

sam_infra: confirmed high concurrency bursts from GalaxyHome IP block. token distribution skewed to long prefixes (avg seq ~ 1500). KV cache hit rate dropped ~60% -> 10% over 2m.

kai_runtime: on runtime side, streaming stalls correlate with frequent cache evictions on host pool gpu-3b. suspect prefix fanout causing asynchronous backpressure.

mike_sre: putting mitigation plan here: 1) throttle client's concurrency to soft-limit 6 connections 2) enable model-fallback to quantized variant for this key 3) bump kv_cache_size on affected nodes 4) capture trace spans and heap snapshots. who can run the throttles?

eric_oncall: @sam_infra can we add a per-key concurrency cap temporarily? also let's enable fallback routing to rwin-4q for GalaxyHome.

sam_infra: yes, running command now. on console:  ```
# temp per-key concurrency
redwoodctl rate-limit set --api-key GH-xxxx --concurrency 6 --duration 30m
# enable fallback
redwoodctl routes override --api-key GH-xxxx --fallback-model rwin-4q --duration 30m
```

deploy-bot: rollout started: route-override for GH-xxxx -> rwin-4q (canary 10% -> 100%). logs: canary healthy.

galaxy_ops: we pushed a traffic spike from our side to test, we saw stalls around 14:03 UTC. thanks for the fast response. we have a background job that fans out long prompts to multiple streams. we can pause that if needed.

eric_oncall: @galaxy_ops please pause the background job for 10m if possible, reduces concurrency and helps KV stabilise. we'll keep you posted.

galaxy_ops: pausing now. ETA to resume ~ 10m.

anya_sre: good. also gathering per-request kv cache keys count and eviction metrics. sending query to metrics: ```
query: sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total{customer="GalaxyHome"}[1m])) by (host)
```

sam_infra: I increased kv_cache_size on pool-gpu-3b hosts by 25% as an emergency patch. Will monitor memory.

kai_runtime: initiating rolling restart of affected runtimes to clear pathological caches and rebalance streams. doing 1/5 at a time.

mike_sre: capturing traces — set span sampling for GH-xxxx to 100% for 15m: ```
tracingctl set-sampling --customer GH-xxxx --rate 1.0 --duration 15m
```

eric_oncall: note: fallback to rwin-4q may change output slightly. notify customer.

galaxy_ops: understood, acceptable for now. priority is stability.

deploy-bot: route-override reached 100% -> all requests now allowed to fallback path.

anya_sre: after throttle + fallback + kv bump we see p99 drop from 9.8s -> 2.1s in the last 2m, p95 back under SLO. still seeing occasional 5-6s spikes during restart windows.

kai_runtime: one host (gpu-3b-07) still showing higher latency, investigating thread dumps.

sam_infra: thread dump shows stuck epoll waits on that host, will reprovision that instance if it doesn't clear in 3m.

mike_sre: opening an incident check-list: impact, mitigation, customer comms, root-cause hypothesis (long-prefix fanout -> kv cache thrash -> eviction storms -> streaming stalls), follow-ups (cap concurrency, model-quantization recommendation, cache tuning, client guidance on prompt sharding).

eric_oncall: customer comms: @galaxy_ops we've applied temporary per-key concurrency limit, fallback routing to a quantized model, and increased cache size. Observed latency back to acceptable levels. We'll keep throttling for 30m and follow up with RCA.

galaxy_ops: appreciated. we'll monitor from our side and keep the background job paused for 10m. please share logs/traces if helpful.

anya_sre: uploading captured traces + perf histogram to incident tracker. saving key metrics snapshot: ```
p95_before: 1.2s, p99_before: 9.8s
p95_after: 0.9s, p99_after: 2.1s
kv_cache_hit_before: 10% kv_cache_hit_after: 72%
```

sam_infra: gpu-3b-07 reprovisioned (restarted container + underlying VM). latency for that host returned to baseline.

kai_runtime: rolling restart completed. monitoring for 10m.

mike_sre: suggestion for postmortem action items: 1) per-customer default concurrency caps 2) autoscaling rules that consider long-prefix distribution 3) better eviction policies (LRU vs TTL hybrid) 4) documented client guidance for GalaxyHome about prompt sharding.

eric_oncall: agreed. I'll create the incident page and assign follow-ups. tagging @product and @ddx for docs + client guidance.

galaxy_ops: thanks team. we saw a clear improvement and will run a few heavy tests tomorrow; please keep the fallback option and throttles in place until we confirm.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied, customer impacted: partial streaming stalls, severity: P2. follow-ups assigned.

eric_oncall: ending active paging. will handoff to next oncall for 1h watch: @anya_sre take over?

anya_sre: taking watch. I'll keep an eye on p99 and KV metrics. ping if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:

galaxy_ops: leaving a note: we will add better backoff in our background job and reduce simultaneous streams. thanks again.

mike_sre: closing notes: evidence points to single-tenant high-concurrency long-prefix workload + cache thrash. temporary mitigations were effective. RCA to follow in incident doc.

eric_oncall: thread closed for active paging. last_message_ts: 3419877200
